invariant: Steady-state energy balance of the boiler component (the part shared by the old and new semantics): let QFue=heat released by the fuel (≥0), Qport=heatPort.Q_flow (positive for environment→boiler), and Hw=m_flow*(h_out-h_in) (heat gained by the working fluid); then the heat carried away by the flue gas E = QFue + Qport - Hw must satisfy 0 ≤ E ≤ QFue; in particular, when y=0 (QFue=0), E=0, i.e. Hw = Qport: when the burner is off, the heat lost by the working fluid exactly equals the heat received by the environment, and energy is neither created from nothing nor destroyed. Applies to energyDynamics=SteadyState (or t→∞ under constant inputs).
convention_note: Whether heat loss is included in efficiency is a convention (the old and new semantics may differ), but 'flue-gas heat ∈ [0, QFue], and when y=0, heat lost by the working fluid=heat gained by the environment' must hold under both conventions and does not depend on the convention
